item.title: Google launches Guided Vision in Gemini Live for real‑time audio descriptions on Android
item.description:
Google launches Guided Vision in Gemini Live for real‑time audio descriptions on Android

Google’s Guided Vision feature debuted today in the Gemini Live app on compatible Android devices, providing real‑time audio descriptions of anything pointed at with the phone’s camera.

🔍 Overview

  • Guided Vision works when you share your camera in Gemini Live.
  • It delivers spoken information about small text, surroundings, objects, and details on specific items.
  • Users can ask follow‑up questions, such as reading an expiration date.

🧩 How it works

  • The phone’s camera feed is processed by Google’s Gemini AI, which generates audio cues to help line up the shot if the target is off‑frame.
  • The system is designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or need situational assistance, similar to Apple’s VoiceOver Live Recognition.

⚙️ Key details

  • Reading fine print – the AI can read small text and fine print.
  • Object identification – it can find or identify objects in the scene.
  • Follow‑up queries – users can ask additional questions about what they see.
  • Audio alignment cues – Gemini provides cues to adjust the camera view.
  • Safety disclaimer – Google advises not to rely on Guided Vision for navigation, safe‑travel guidance, obstacle detection, or as a substitute for a cane or mobility aid.

🚀 Availability

  • Integrated in the Gemini Live app.
  • Also available through Google TalkBack.
  • Can be enabled via an accessibility shortcut in the Settings app on Android 9 and above, following recent Pixel updates.

💡 Why it matters

Guided Vision extends AI‑powered visual assistance to Android users, offering a new way for low‑vision individuals to access information about their environment without additional hardware.

#Google #Accessibility #AI #GuidedVision

Source: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print

item.title: University Startups Launches Trinity AI to Assist Students with Disability Transition Planning
item.description:
University Startups Launches Trinity AI to Assist Students with Disability Transition Planning

Trinity is a conversational AI solution developed by University Startups to assist students with disabilities in taking ownership of their postsecondary and Individualized Education Program (IEP) planning.

🧩 How it works

University Startups utilized g/d/n/a to build a fully serverless architecture on AWS. The system utilizes a multi-agent solution powered by Amazon Bedrock and Claude 3.5 Sonnet to provide targeted guidance.

The architecture employs a hierarchical six-agent system:

Agent Function
Orchestrator Agent Reads student conversation, selects the right path, sequences agents, and consolidates final output
College Agent Recommends 4-year universities and community colleges from an over 30,000 record Knowledge Base
Employment Agent Matches jobs and career pathways from an over 1,000 occupation Knowledge Base
Training Agent Recommends vocational programs and certifications

⚙️ Key details

The platform includes accessibility features such as Amazon Polly for text-to-speech and Amazon Transcribe for speech-to-text. Data security is maintained through compliance with HIPAA and FERPA standards, while Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are used for content filtering and hallucination reduction.

🚀 Availability

Trinity reached educators and students across more than a dozen U.S. states within its first year. International expansion into Saudi Arabia and Kuwait is now underway.

#ArtificialIntelligence #EdTech #AWS #Accessibility #SpecialEducation

Source: Trinity: Agentic AI-powered transition planning for students with disabilities | Amazon Web Services
